page: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz on the arm64 architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides one thread per core without hyperthreading, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 672 GB, providing an allocation of 7.0 GB per vCPU. The instance also includes 5,669 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage, though it includes no discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight notable strengths in parallel computation and data throughput. In synthetic memory tests, the architecture achieves 465.42 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 205.78 GB/sec in writes, placing its memory subsystem in the top 10 percent of tested cloud servers. The system also scored in the top tier for multi-threaded Geekbench compute (23,825.0), Clang compilation (75,157.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (857.84 GB/sec). Storage-adjacent and transactional benchmarks are equally strong, evidenced by top-tier PassMark database operations (37,968.9) and high-throughput Redis performance reaching 170.49 million SET operations per second.

Architectural tradeoffs center primarily on single-threaded versus multi-threaded performance. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core (1,689.0) and stress-ng single-core (2,073.39), remain in the average tier. Consequently, the instance derives its processing capabilities from massive thread density rather than individual core velocity. Qualitatively, the density of 96 physical cores coupled with bundled NVMe storage delivers high resource efficiency for high-concurrency environments, reducing the necessity of provisioning external high-IOPS storage tiers for temporary scratch space.

The E96pds_v6 is primarily suited for large in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, and real-time data ingestion pipelines. Its capacity to handle 99.91 GB/sec of static web serving throughput and rapid multi-threaded operations also positions it well for large-scale enterprise microservices, high-volume ETL processing, and distributed software builds.
description: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 96 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores operating at 3.4 GHz. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture, it provides 672 GB of system memory alongside 5,669 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark testing shows top-tier multi-core execution and memory throughput, with uncached memory read bandwidth reaching 465.42 GB/sec and Redis SET performance surpassing 170 million operations per second. While single-thread speeds remain within standard mid-tier parameters, the dedicated physical core topology eliminates hyperthreading contention across concurrent tasks. The generous ratio of 7.0 GB of memory per core and high local IOPS capacity offer balanced resource efficiency for memory-heavy setups. This configuration is well-suited for enterprise-grade relational databases, distributed caching layers, continuous software build environments, and large-scale data transformation workflows.
